newsitem.title: UK: RUSSIA DEBT ADVANCES FURTHER, BRADYS MOSTLY WEAKER.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA DEBT ADVANCES FURTHER, BRADYS MOSTLY WEAKER.

text.p: Russian loans continued their bull run on Friday, but prices for most other emerging debt slipped back in line with weaker U.S. Treasuries.
Dealers said investors remained enthusiastic about Russian paper on growing confidence that Moscow will close a deal with London Club of commercial bank creditors well before year-end.
Dollar-denominated Russian Vneshekonombank loans RUVNUSLNS=RR added 3/4 to 101-5/8 bid after trading above par for the first time on Thursday.
"Going through the par level has been quite a big psychological breakthrough," said one dealer.
But dealers said volumes were down on Thursday as the rise in the U.S. long bond yield back above 6.50 percent caused players to pause.
"Today seems much quieter. I think people are taking a breather because the long bond has now broken through 6.50 again and talk is of a new range of 6.50-6.60," said one.
Russian PRINs RUPRIN=RR also pushed to new highs, adding 3/8 to 73-3/8 and IANs RUIAN=RR were up 1/4 to 80-3/4.
But key Latin American issues were off with weaker Treasuries as the market took a wait-and-see approach before key U.S. data next week.

U.S. July Atlanta Fed index, second-quarter productivity and unit labor costs and the Richmond Fed's July survey are due on Tuesday. U.S. July retail sales and key inflation figures are also due next week.
Brazil "C" bonds BRD8D14=RR were off one point at 83-3/8 while Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR dipped 1/8 to 95-3/8.
In Eastern Europe, Bulgarian FRBs BGFLIRB=RR shed 3/8 to 63-5/8.
